summary: Alexander County, NC: a Forest Service fire tower on Linney's Mountain, staffed in spring 1972; no build date, later history or current status found.

events.note: Forest Service operated the tower from mid-February, with a smoke spotter stationed until about mid-May; from a March 16, 1972 newspaper item as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts site

evidence.supports: Forest Service operated the fire tower from mid-February, smoke spotter until about mid-May, 1972
evidence.quote: The forest service has been operating its fire tower at Linney's Mountain since mid-February and will continue to have the smoke spotter stationed there until about mid-May, the worst period for forest fires.

evidence.supports: item taken from the Statesville Record & Landmark
page files the tower under Alexander County
page lists the tower under a National Forest heading, naming no forest
tower on the state list at 35.92889, -81.16333 in Alexander County

notes_for_editor: Only dated source is a 1972 newspaper item as transcribed by the Forest Lookouts site; the Statesville Record & Landmark original was not checked. No build date, design, height, fate or current status found, so status, access and visit stay unknown. The record stores the tnlandforms code FA5410 as an NGS register entry; no source explains that code, so it was not treated as a lookout register. A search snippet (an Alexander County Facebook post, not readable here) mentions a Linney Mountain Tower planned as a broadband point-of-presence site, which may mean a communications structure stands there now. Unverified and not used in the story. Check on the ground or with NC Forest Service records before adding a today section.
